question: Which statement best describes Lexical scope?
options: When a variable is used, the engine looks in the current scope, then the parent scope, then its parent, and so on — a lookup path called the scope chain. A closure keeps a reference to that chain, so the inner function can still read the outer variables later. It does not copy the values; it references the live variables.

A closure is most visible when an inner function outlives its parent — typically by being returned or passed as a callback. Even though the parent has finished executing, the inner function still holds onto the parent's variables. This is the mechanism behind callbacks, event handlers, and factory functions.

Because the outer variables are only reachable through the inner function, closures let you create truly private state that callers cannot touch directly. This is how the module pattern and counter factories hide their internals while exposing a small API.

JavaScript resolves variables by where functions are written in the source, not where they are called. A function can 'see' variables declared in its own body and in every enclosing function, all the way up to the global scope. This static, author-time relationship is what makes closures predictable.
